page: Microsoft Azure M16bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The platform is driven by a dedicated 4.0 GHz Intel Xeon 8473C processor with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware capabilities include 105 MB of L3 cache as well as hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU. Local temporary storage includes a 429 GB solid-state drive with support for Premium Storage block volumes, without discrete GPU hardware attached.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded compute metrics, led by a Geekbench single-core score of 2196.0, single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 32.97 GB/sec, and strong text processing performance. Parallel performance operates in the expected median range, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 13388.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 16883.26. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 107.61 GB/sec for reads and 68.03 GB/sec for writes. Under CPU-based machine learning inference, the instance displays strong generation throughput for small language models at 303.34 tokens per second.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the M16bds_v3 provides solid cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM without demanding high vCPU counts. A clear architectural tradeoff is the moderate multi-threaded throughput compared to compute-focused instance lines, alongside the ephemeral nature of the bundled 429 GB local SSD, which necessitates network-attached storage for persistent operational state. This configuration fits enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, moderate ETL jobs, and memory-constrained analytical workloads.
